key_insight: Better reliability diagnostics do not necessarily improve materials screening; their value depends on whether they reduce DFT evaluations while preserving required recall of near-hull candidates.
engineering_relevance: Evaluate MLIP reliability interventions against screening outcomes and information-acquisition costs, not prediction metrics alone.
method: Rank candidate crystal structures with MACE-MP, CHGNet, and Orb V3 before DFT verification.
Test novelty detection, sparse DFT calibration, and chemistry-level ranking audits.
Measure DFT savings at required near-hull recall and use two-oracle analysis to diagnose decision alignment.
evidence_signal: Across the three interventions, improved diagnostic performance did not reliably translate into better screening: novelty weakly ranked failure severity, calibration could leave screening unchanged or worse, and audits did not yield robustly beneficial routing.
watch_item: Results depend on the screening objective: perfect average-ranking information can misguide formation-energy screening, while finite-budget audits still failed to realize oracle value in the evaluated hull-aligned variant.
paper_title: Diagnostic Accuracy Is Not Deployment Value: Decision-Aligned Reliability Evaluation for Foundation MLIPs in Materials Discovery
